Two of them pump blood to the gills, while the third sends blood to the rest of the body. Even cooler: the main heart actually *stops beating* when they swim! 

Want to hear another random fact, or would you rather dive into one of your suggested topics? I'm ready for whatever you choose!

Did you know that a day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus? Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate on its axis once, but it only takes around 225 Earth days for Venus to orbit the Sun. Isn't that amazing?

* Exoplanets are planets that orbit stars outside our solar system. The first exoplanet was discovered in 1992, and since then, thousands of exoplanets have been found.
* Exoplanets are detected using various methods, including the transit method (which measures the dimming of a star as a planet passes in front of it), the radial velocity method (which measures the wobble of a star caused by the gravitational pull of an orbiting planet), and direct imaging (which involves taking a picture of the planet).
* The search for exoplanets is an active area of research, with new discoveries being made all the time. Some of the most exciting recent discoveries include the TRAPPIST-1 system, which contains seven Earth-sized planets orbiting a nearby star, and the discovery of potentially habitable exoplanets in the habitable zone of their stars.
